claim: A2A is the standard card 1.5 Agent-to-Agent is checked against: it defines how one agent asks another for work without either exposing its internals.
query: A2A protocol specification purpose interoperability opaque agents
snippet: The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol is an open standard designed to facilitate communication and interoperability between independent, potentially opaque AI agent systems.
title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
topic: What A2A is and what it is for

claim: The verb set is named by the standard and is binding-independent: Send Message, Send Streaming Message, Get Task, List Tasks, Cancel Task, Subscribe to Task, four push-notification-config operations, and Get Extended Agent Card.
query: A2A core operations independent of protocol binding
snippet: The following operations define the fundamental capabilities that all A2A implementations must support, independent of the specific protocol binding used.
title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
topic: The operation set every implementation must support

claim: The state domain is enumerated by the standard and split into terminal and interrupted, which is what a caller must branch on.
query: A2A TaskState terminal interrupted states blocking behaviour
snippet: The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state (`TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, `TASK_STATE_FAILED`, `TASK_STATE_CANCELED`, `TASK_STATE_REJECTED`) or an interrupted state (`TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED`, `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`) before returning.
title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
topic: Task state domain, terminal and interrupted

claim: The standard names its own typed errors rather than leaving failure to the binding; nine A2A-specific errors are tabled, each with the condition that raises it.
query: A2A specific errors task not found not cancelable unsupported operation
snippet: `TaskNotCancelableError`              | An attempt was made to cancel a task that is not in a cancelable state
title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
topic: Typed failures at the agent-to-agent boundary
